Abstract.AbstractText: Cow's milk allergy affects approximately 2 to 3% of children under 3 years. Allergic reactions often occur at an early onset within the first months of age [1]. In 80 to 85% of the described cases a natural tolerance develops until the age of 5 years. However, a proportion of 1% of adults remain cow's milk allergic, often associated with severe reactions [2]. Some breast-fed babies with cow's milk allergy still show symptoms despite a strict cow's milk-free diet of the nursing mother, and they react until the mother discontinues breast feeding.
